title: In This Town, Count Your Shadows

lines.text: In this town, when the streetlights come on, you count your shadows.
If you have two,
one of them isn't yours.
We call it the Tagalong. It follows you home.
And if it reaches your front door, it comes in with you.
So every kid in this town looks down at every lamp.
Mr. Pell found two shadows on his way home once.
He came home different. His curtains have been shut ever since.
But there's one way to lose it.
Shadows can't live in total darkness.
Stand in the dark, count to ten, and the extra one lets go.
Just make sure the one that comes back out is yours.
I walked home alone from violin every Thursday.
Six lamps between the school and my door.
At the third lamp, I looked down.
Two shadows.
And one of them turned its head when I didn't.
I ran. It kept up with me on the snow, the whole way.
Two lamps from home, there was a broken one.
Pitch black underneath.
I stood in the dark and counted.
One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
Then I stepped back into the light.
One shadow.
I waved, and it waved back.
I ran the rest of the way and slammed the door behind me.
That night, I reached up to turn off my lamp.
My shadow on the wall reached up too.
A second late.
And when I put my hand down, it didn't.
It never had to follow me home.
It came in as my shadow.
